title: A urine concentration interaction does not reliably improve nocturia prediction across NHANES samples
abstract: A source-frozen weighted logistic model trained in4572 NHANES2009–2010 adults was tested in3924 separately sampled2011–2012 adults. Adding a log urine-osmolality by log urine-creatinine interaction beyond flexible additive concentrations, routine serum biochemistry and demographics changed target Brier score0.15808562 to0.15806843. Rescaled PSU-bootstrap95% delta interval[-0.00009392,+0.00005301] crossed zero; source/target coefficient-refit uncertainty also crossed zero. Weaker-penalty and subgroup checks changed the sign. This one feature failed the prespecified superiority criterion; no equivalence, causal, clinical utility or independent-study validation claim. Reproducible offline analysis, numerical author check and exact clean rerun are supplied.
